heroHeadline: Madrid Approves €309M Emergency Decree as Police Report Alleges Moroccan Agents Guided the Ceuta Crossing
heroSubtitle: Spain's Council of Ministers approved a €309 million emergency decree-law plus €50 million in loan guarantees for Ceuta's security, minors' care, businesses and services, alongside confirmation that reception capacity has more than doubled to over 3,400 places in a week. The same day, National Police intelligence told the investigating judge that uniformed Moroccan gendarmes and plainclothes agents actively guided the July 30-31 crossing toward Ceuta — a claim that prompted a three-hour meeting between King Felipe VI and PM Sánchez, notable after the King was excluded from the prior Security Council session. A separate government analysis found relocating Ceuta's roughly 2,678 migrant minors at the current pace would take nearly four years. On Sept 2, Ceuta's own local holiday was overshadowed as PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo led nationwide solidarity protests — after Madrid's government delegation denied a permit for the Cibeles rally he and Vox's Santiago Abascal attended anyway — one day ahead of Sánchez's Sept 3 Congress appearance on the crisis.
